title: Paper and Lean correspondence review
subtitle: Publication claims and exact formal statements

exact.label: exact
exact.meaning: The Lean statement says what the paper says (up to notation).

equivalent.label: equivalent
equivalent.meaning: Different formulation (e.g. prime spectrum instead of point set, left instead of right coefficients); the equivalence is explained on the card.

lean-stronger.label: Lean stronger
lean-stronger.meaning: Lean proves a more general statement (e.g. any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, n ≥ 0); the paper statement is a special case.

partial.label: partial
partial.meaning: Only part of the paper statement, or a neighbouring statement, is formalized.

paper-wrong.label: paper wrong
paper-wrong.meaning: The paper statement is false or ill-typed as printed; Lean proves the corrected statement that the argument actually needs.

unverifiable.label: not checkable here
unverifiable.meaning: Claims about artefacts outside the audited repositories.

same.label: same
same.meaning: Lean follows the paper proof step by step.

similar.label: similar
similar.meaning: Same idea; Lean reorganises or makes steps explicit.

different.label: different
different.meaning: Lean proves the statement by a different argument; the paper proof itself is not machine-checked.

lean-only.label: proved in Lean only
lean-only.meaning: The paper cites the result; Lean contains a full proof.

unformalized.label: unformalized
unformalized.meaning: Paper proof with no formal counterpart.

critical.label: critical
critical.meaning: A printed statement is false, or a claimed conclusion is not established. (None threatens Theorem 1.1, whose Lean proof is independent.)

major.label: major
major.meaning: Real gap or false step that needs a new argument or a rewrite of the passage.

minor.label: minor
minor.meaning: Local fix: missing hypothesis, justification, or citation.

note.label: note
note.meaning: Information for the reviewer, no change required.

review_checks.label: Lean statement matches (or relation is as stated)
Proposed publication statement matches a proved endpoint with the same hypotheses and conclusion
